verbalization: The visible evidence suggests that neomycin may interact with Macrophage-expressed gene 1 protein through multiple indirect pathways. The first pathway links neomycin to Multidrug resistance-associated protein 7, which is then targeted by Epifriedelin, ultimately leading to the expression of the Macrophage-expressed gene 1 protein. The second pathway connects neomycin to Induced myeloid leukemia cell differentiation protein Mcl-1, which is targeted by 1-(3-Methylbutyryl)Phloroglucinol-Glucopyranoside, also leading to the expression of the same gene. Both pathways involve molecular interactions that modulate gene expression, suggesting that neomycin may influence the expression of Macrophage-expressed gene 1 protein through different molecular mechanisms. The evidence is consistent with a role for neomycin in modulating gene expression in macrophages, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
